acceptance: Context records `sum_ratio` and `speed_factor` for at least 30 PR runs measured against the 2026-11-26 baseline (`f2ff4d7` or later), at least 5 of them with speed factor ≥ 1.4, and the correlation between the two.

A fix lands that, replayed over those runs, blocks no run whose pull request leaves the fast tier unchanged. A seeded +400 s summed slowdown is still blocked at speed factors near 0.8, 1.5 and 1.9. Otherwise the owner records a decision to accept the measured false-block rate, and the gate docs carry a worked example of the normalizer's limits.
Any threshold, ceiling or normalizer change was shown to the owner with these figures before it was committed.
context:
2026-11-11: merged duplicate ci-fast-duration-gate-slow-runner-margin-20261101 into this item. Slow-runner evidence from that item: of 59 post-flip verdicts, 15 ran with a runner speed factor >= 1.5 (up to 1.95) and 8 had a summed ratio above 1.20 (max 1.282 vs the 1.30 limit); 7 of 59 exceeded the 360 s delta term alone. #4002 (deleting tests only) got would-block at 1.313 / +442.6 s with a median per-test ratio of 1.010. Acceptance should cover both a false would-block on a slow runner and a real slowdown hidden by a slow runner.

2026-11-21 finding from #4410, appended 2026-11-22 on the owner's decision: CI run 44796776942 failed the fast duration gate at a summed ratio of 1.321 on a runner whose calibration rated it 1.537x, then passed on a full rerun. Before the calibration adjustment the tests were faster than baseline, so the failure came from the normalizer on a slow-rated runner, not from the change. This is the high-calibration false block this item describes. Related record with the per-runner-class method and figures: fast-duration-gate-runner-class-spread-20261120.

2026-11-26, after the refreshed baseline merged (#4477, `f2ff4d7`). These are PR verdicts from the `fast-duration-verdict` artifacts:

| Runner speed factor | Summed ratio | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0.71 | 0.943 | pass |
| 0.81 | 1.165 | pass |

| 1.44 | 1.439 | would-block: #4541, run 45864043111 attempt 1, head `26231eb337`, delta +617.8 s |

- **Run 45864043111:**
  - attempt 2 (full rerun) passed the fast-duration gate, but `core` failed on a cancelled Windows framing job;
  - attempt 3 re-ran only the failed jobs and passed;
  - #4541 then merged.
- **Before the refresh:** two #4541 runs on the old baseline breached the absolute ceiling: 1,782.2 s and 1,764.0 s against 1,755.5 s.
- **After normalization:** between a run at speed factor 0.87 and one at 1.51, `new_test_seconds` moved from 158.1 s to 178.2 s, with three new tests.
- So both terms of the gate stay dependent on runner speed.

Decision gates and guardrails added 2026-11-26:
- **Gate:** the owner approves any change to `VERIFY_RATIO_THRESHOLD`, `VERIFY_DELTA_SECONDS`, the ceiling file or the normalizer before it is committed, with these figures attached.
- **Guardrail:** never regenerate or hand-edit the baseline to clear a would-block.
- **Guardrail:** never re-run CI to turn a would-block into a pass, except one rerun when the verdict artifact shows speed factor ≥ 1.4. Record both runs here. A rerun of a job the runner cancelled or never started does not count.
description: For core PR 3562 the fast-tier verdict was would-block with a normalized summed ratio of 1.156 although the PR's own tests added 0.08s. The run's calibration factor was 1.84, most excess was first-in-worker import cost spread over unrelated tests, and an offline verify of the old head's artifact against a freshly built baseline raised the ratio to 1.196. The baseline was regenerated to lift the refusal, which hides the cause.
